_comment: Capability-root manifest for comms/ (founder ruling oyatie-0s8). This is the ADR-0562 capability's OWN service manifest, the `<root>/manifest.json` shape that ci/facade/service-tier-metadata treats as top-level. It exists because the capability-first rehome left 24 crates directly under comms/ that belonged to NO manifest: the sub-service manifests under comms/*/manifest.json cover their own services only. Every crate, service and SLO path below was read off the tree, not transcribed.
dr_tier_derivation: Strictest dr_tier declared by any absorbed service of this capability (comms-email=T0, contact-center=T1, emergency=T3, mail=T0, meet=T0, messenger=T0). The shared crates sit in the failure path of the strictest consumer, so the capability root may not claim a weaker DR class than the service that depends on it.

substrate_dag_position._note: ADR-0562 capability-registry declares comms tier=substrate stratum=S2; all six absorbed services declare the same value.

purpose: Communications substrate capability root. The crates directly under comms/ are the shared mail, messenger, meet, calendar and address-book domain/usecase model, its port boundaries, its REST/gRPC facades and its Postgres adapters. The deployed comms services (comms-email, contact-center, emergency, mail, meet, messenger) carry their own manifests, SLOs and contracts.

bounded_contexts.name: comms-adapters
bounded_contexts.description: Capability-level driven adapters (storage, transport, provider) under comms/adapters/. Covered by no service manifest before this file existed.

bounded_contexts.name: comms-core
bounded_contexts.description: Capability-level domain / usecase / kernel crates (pure, no I/O) under comms/core/. Covered by no service manifest before this file existed.

bounded_contexts.name: comms-facade
bounded_contexts.description: Capability-level composition, app and evidence crates under comms/facade/. Covered by no service manifest before this file existed.

bounded_contexts.name: comms-ports
bounded_contexts.description: Capability-level port + API boundary crates under comms/ports/. Covered by no service manifest before this file existed.

contracts_non_claim: This capability root serves no endpoint of its own, so all three carrier arrays are EMPTY rather than populated: every OpenAPI, AsyncAPI and proto contract under comms/ belongs to one of the absorbed services listed above and is declared by that service's manifest. The internal_grpc block is present-and-empty, not omitted, because the H2/proto3 posture binds any internal gRPC this capability may later expose (ADR-0056/0105 zero-GraphQL, internal-only Protobuf); an omitted block would read as an unruled surface.

adrs.title: Closed Capability Registry And Deterministic Placement

sharding_automation.non_claim: A capability root of library crates has no tenant shards to split, merge or rebalance. Sharding automation is claimed by the absorbed services that actually run, in their own manifests; ADR-0348 automation is declared disabled here rather than omitted so the absence is a measured statement instead of a gap.

dr.non_claim: No runtime store, failover drill or DR evidence belongs to this capability root; DR is exercised by the absorbed services. `dr_tier` above is the inherited obligation, not a measured result.

foundation_non_claims: this manifest describes the 24 crates directly under comms/ and does NOT restate, aggregate or supersede the 6 absorbed service manifests listed above
no deployed process, served endpoint, measured benchmark, capacity telemetry or audit-chain writer is claimed for the capability root itself

slo_exemption.rationale: The comms/core, comms/ports, comms/adapters and comms/facade crates are capability-level libraries and transport facades with no deployed process of their own, so no measured runtime SLI exists for them; the six deployed comms services carry their own OpenSLO files under comms/*/slos/ and comms/observability/slos/. This root manifest is an accounting surface for the shared crates, not a restatement of service SLO coverage.
slo_exemption.evidence: comms/observability/slos/ — the capability's OpenSLO files all sit under a per-service subdirectory there, none at capability level, which is the measured statement that no SLI belongs to the root crates
